description: VN 'nói (với) tôi' transfer: Vietnamese 'nói' collapses say & tell, so learners write 'say me the news' where English ditransitive reporting to a person needs 'tell + indirect object' ('tell me the news'). Rule en-vietlish-say-tell-person maps say/says/said/saying -> tell/tells/told/telling ONLY before the unambiguous object pronouns me/us, preserving case, and abstains on fronted what/which questions.
fp_risk_note: Low-medium risk. Object scope is locked to me/us only. you/him/her/them/it are deliberately excluded because they yield valid English: embedded subject ('say you are right'), possessive ('say her name'), utter-object ('just say them'). 'say with me' is owned by en-calque-say-with-person (a 'with' between the verb and pronoun means this rule never matches it); 'say to me' is already correct (the 'to' breaks adjacency); fronted 'What did you say?' has no indirect object and abstains; 'Say hello' has no pronoun IO.

positive.input: Can you say me the answer
positive.expectedCorrection: Can you tell me the answer?
positive.notes: Question 'say me' -> 'tell me'; co-fires with en-question-form-final-mark for the '?'.

negative.notes: Already correct: 'to' between verb and pronoun breaks adjacency -> must abstain.
Fronted what-question, no indirect object; mirrors say-with's what/which guard -> must abstain.
No pronoun indirect object ('hello' is the utterance) -> must abstain.
Owned by en-calque-say-with-person ('with' between verb and pronoun); this rule must NOT fire. Engine still corrects via the calque rule.
'you' excluded (embedded clause subject, not an indirect object) -> must abstain.
'her' excluded (possessive determiner, not an indirect object) -> must abstain.
